series.name: Liberty Cap
series.description: The smallest US denomination. 1793 faces left; 1794–1797 faces right.

series.name: Draped Bust
series.description: Robert Scot's Draped Bust portrait.

series.name: Classic Head
series.description: John Reich's Classic Head. 1831 and 1836 are mostly proofs and restrikes.

series.name: Braided Hair
series.description: Christian Gobrecht's Braided Hair. 1840–1848 and 1852 were struck only as proofs, so the folder starts at 1849.

series.name: Flowing Hair Large Cent
series.description: The first cents struck by the US Mint, with chain and then wreath reverses.

series.name: Liberty Cap Large Cent
series.description: Liberty with a cap on a pole behind her head.

series.name: Draped Bust Large Cent
series.description: Robert Scot's Draped Bust. 1799 and 1804 are the key dates.

series.name: Classic Head Large Cent
series.description: John Reich's Classic Head.

series.name: Coronet (Matron Head) Large Cent
series.description: Liberty wearing a coronet. No cents were dated 1815.

series.name: Braided Hair Large Cent
series.description: Gobrecht's Braided Hair, the last of the large cents.

series.name: Flying Eagle
series.description: The first small cent, in copper-nickel. 1856 was a pattern given out to officials.

series.name: Indian Head
series.description: James Longacre's Indian Head. Copper-nickel until 1864, then bronze. 1908-S and 1909-S are the only branch-mint issues.

series.name: Lincoln Wheat
series.description: Victor David Brenner's Lincoln portrait with two wheat ears on the reverse. 1943 cents are zinc-coated steel.

series.name: Lincoln Memorial
series.description: Frank Gasparro's Lincoln Memorial reverse. Copper until mid-1982, copper-plated zinc after, which is why 1982 has seven slots. 1965–1967 coins carry no mint mark.

series.name: Lincoln Bicentennial
series.description: Four reverses for the 200th anniversary of Lincoln's birth, one for each stage of his life.

series.name: Lincoln Shield
series.description: Union shield reverse by Lyndall Bass. 2017 Philadelphia cents are the only ones with a P mint mark. Circulation strikes ended in November 2025.

series.name: Shield
series.description: The first US coin to carry IN GOD WE TRUST. 1873 was struck only as a proof.

series.name: Silver (Trime)
series.description: The smallest US silver coin, made to buy three-cent postage stamps. 1851-O is the only branch-mint issue.

series.name: Nickel
series.description: Copper-nickel three cents. 1877, 1878 and 1886 were struck only as proofs.

series.name: Flowing Hair
series.description: The first silver five-cent pieces.

series.name: Draped Bust, Small Eagle
series.description: Robert Scot's Draped Bust with a small eagle on a cloud.

series.name: Draped Bust, Heraldic Eagle
series.description: The heraldic eagle reverse, copied from the Great Seal.

series.name: Capped Bust
series.description: William Kneass's version of the Capped Bust.

series.name: Seated Liberty
series.description: Gobrecht's Seated Liberty, through no stars, stars, arrows and legend types.

series.name: Shield, With Rays
series.description: The first copper-nickel five-cent piece, with rays between the stars on the reverse.

series.name: Shield, No Rays
series.description: Rays removed because they made the coins hard to strike. 1877 and 1878 were proofs only.

series.name: Liberty Head
series.description: Charles Barber's V nickel. The first 1883 coins left off the word CENTS.

series.name: Buffalo, Type 1
series.description: The bison stands on a raised mound. The FIVE CENTS on the mound wore away fast, so it was changed within months.

series.name: Buffalo, Type 2
series.description: The mound is cut down to a flat line with FIVE CENTS recessed below it.

series.name: Jefferson
series.description: Felix Schlag's Jefferson with Monticello. 1942–1945 wartime nickels are 35% silver and carry a large mint mark over Monticello, including the first P.

series.name: Westward Journey
series.description: Four designs for the bicentennial of the Louisiana Purchase and the Lewis and Clark expedition.

series.name: Return to Monticello
series.description: Jamie Franki's forward-facing Jefferson with Monticello restored to the reverse.

series.name: Draped Bust, Small Eagle
series.description: Robert Scot's Draped Bust with a small eagle on a cloud.

series.name: Draped Bust, Heraldic Eagle
series.description: The heraldic eagle reverse.

series.name: Capped Bust, Large Size
series.description: John Reich's Capped Bust, struck on the open-collar press.

series.name: Capped Bust, Small Size
series.description: Struck in a close collar from 1828, giving a smaller, uniform coin.

series.name: Seated Liberty
series.description: Gobrecht's Seated Liberty, with arrows at the date in 1853–1855 and 1873–1874 for weight changes.

series.name: Barber
series.description: Charles Barber's Liberty Head. The 1894-S, with 24 struck, is one of the great US rarities.

series.name: Winged Liberty (Mercury)
series.description: Adolph Weinman's Liberty in a winged cap, often mistaken for Mercury. 1916-D is the key date.

series.name: Roosevelt, Silver
series.description: John Sinnock's Roosevelt in 90% silver.

series.name: Roosevelt, Clad
series.description: Copper-nickel clad. Philadelphia dimes carry a P from 1980; a few 1982 dimes were struck without it.

series.name: Seated Liberty
series.description: Too close in size to the quarter and dropped after two years. 1877 and 1878 were proofs only; the 1876-CC is a great rarity.

series.name: Draped Bust, Small Eagle
series.description: The first US quarter. Only 6,146 were struck.

series.name: Draped Bust, Heraldic Eagle
series.description: The heraldic eagle reverse.

series.name: Capped Bust, Large Size
series.description: John Reich's Capped Bust with E PLURIBUS UNUM on a scroll.

series.name: Capped Bust, Small Size
series.description: William Kneass's reduced quarter, struck in a close collar without the motto.

series.name: Seated Liberty
series.description: Gobrecht's Seated Liberty. Arrows and rays in 1853, arrows 1854–1855 and 1873–1874, IN GOD WE TRUST added in 1866.

series.name: Barber
series.description: Charles Barber's Liberty Head. 1896-S, 1901-S and 1913-S are the key dates.

series.name: Standing Liberty, Type 1
series.description: Hermon MacNeil's original design with Liberty's bare breast.

series.name: Standing Liberty, Type 2
series.description: Liberty's chest covered in mail and the eagle raised, with three stars moved below it. From 1925 the date is recessed so it wears less.

series.name: Washington, Silver
series.description: John Flanagan's Washington in 90% silver. 1932-D and 1932-S are the key dates.

series.name: Washington, Clad
series.description: Copper-nickel clad. No quarters are dated 1975; those years are in the Bicentennial folder.

series.name: Washington, Bicentennial
series.description: Jack Ahr's colonial drummer boy, struck in 1975 and 1976 and all dated 1776–1976.

series.name: 50 State Quarters
series.description: Five states a year, in the order they joined the Union.

series.name: DC and Territories
series.description: An extra year added to honor the District of Columbia and the five US territories.

series.name: America the Beautiful
series.description: One national park or site from each state and territory.

slots.sub: Frank Church River of No Return

slots.label: 2019-D
slots.sub: Frank Church River of No Return

series.name: Crossing the Delaware
series.description: Washington crossing the Delaware, a one-year design between programs.

series.name: American Women
series.description: Five women a year, with Laura Gardin Fraser's Washington portrait.

series.name: Flowing Hair
series.description: The first US half dollars.

series.name: Draped Bust, Small Eagle
series.description: Only about 3,900 were struck, making it one of the rarest US types.

series.name: Draped Bust, Heraldic Eagle
series.description: The heraldic eagle reverse.

series.name: Capped Bust, Lettered Edge
series.description: John Reich's Capped Bust with FIFTY CENTS OR HALF A DOLLAR on the edge. No halves are dated 1816.

series.name: Capped Bust, Reeded Edge
series.description: Smaller coins struck on the new steam press, with a reeded edge and a new denomination on the reverse.

series.name: Seated Liberty
series.description: Gobrecht's Seated Liberty. Arrows and rays in 1853, arrows 1854–1855 and 1873–1874, motto added in 1866.

series.name: Barber
series.description: Charles Barber's Liberty Head.

series.name: Walking Liberty
series.description: Adolph Weinman's Walking Liberty. In 1917 the mint mark moved from the obverse to the reverse.

series.name: Franklin
series.description: John Sinnock's Benjamin Franklin with the Liberty Bell.

series.name: Kennedy
series.description: Gilroy Roberts's Kennedy. 90% silver in 1964, 40% silver 1965–1970, clad after. 1970-D was only in mint sets. No halves are dated 1975.

series.name: Kennedy, Bicentennial
series.description: Seth Huntington's Independence Hall reverse, dated 1776–1976.

series.name: Flowing Hair
series.description: The first US silver dollars. About 1,758 were struck in 1794.

series.name: Draped Bust, Small Eagle
series.description: Robert Scot's Draped Bust with a small eagle on a cloud.

series.name: Draped Bust, Heraldic Eagle
series.description: The heraldic eagle reverse. The famous 1804 dollar was struck decades later as a proof.

series.name: Seated Liberty
series.description: Gobrecht's Seated Liberty with a heraldic eagle; IN GOD WE TRUST added in 1866. 1858 was struck only as a proof.

series.name: Trade Dollar
series.description: Heavier than a regular dollar, made for trade in China. Most later carry Chinese merchants' chop marks.

series.name: Morgan
series.description: George T. Morgan's Liberty Head. Carson City (CC) coins and the 1893-S and 1895 are the famous keys. 1895 Philadelphia is known only as a proof.

series.name: Peace
series.description: Anthony de Francisci's Peace dollar. The 1921 is in high relief.

series.name: Eisenhower
series.description: Frank Gasparro's Eisenhower with the Apollo 11 eagle landing on the Moon. None are dated 1975.

series.name: Eisenhower, Bicentennial
series.description: Dennis Williams's Liberty Bell over the Moon. Type 1 has thick lettering on the reverse, Type 2 thinner lettering.

series.name: Susan B. Anthony
series.description: The first small-size dollar. 1981 coins were only in mint sets; 1999 was struck when Sacagawea dollars were delayed.

series.name: Sacagawea
series.description: Glenna Goodacre's Sacagawea and her son, on a golden manganese-brass coin.

series.name: Presidential
series.description: Four presidents a year in the order they served, with the date and motto on the edge.

series.name: Native American
series.description: The Sacagawea obverse with a new reverse each year honoring Native American contributions.

series.name: American Innovation
series.description: One innovation from each state, in the order they joined the Union.

series.name: Maple Twig, Elizabeth II
series.description: G.E. Kruger Gray's maple twig reverse (his KG initials sit beside it). Round bronze cents from the start of Elizabeth II's reign until the 12-sided cent of 1982. 1967 swapped the twig for Alex Colville's centennial rock dove.

series.name: Madara Rider
series.description: The Madara Rider, an 8th-century rock relief of a horseman spearing a lion, on the coins of the redenominated lev. The date is on the value side.

series.name: Meiji Dragon
series.description: Copper 2 sen with a coiled dragon inside a beaded ring. The date is written in Meiji era years around the rim, read from 大日本 on the left over the top: Meiji 14 is 明治十四年.
